findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes with TypeError when used with datetime ordering
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key is copied from the numeric Paginator and does math.floor/math.ceil on the raw attribute value. Its only caller, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, uses it with order_by="-datetime", so the value is a datetime and math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError. build_cursor calls get_item_key on every non-empty page, so any request with optimized_pagination=true that returns at least one audit log row will 500. Additionally, value_from_cursor returns the raw numeric cursor value, so even if the first page worked, page 2 would compare a timestamp column against a float in the extra WHERE clause and raise a database error. The class needs DateTimePaginator-style key conversion (or should subclass DateTimePaginator). No test covers this path, which is why it wasn't caught.

findings.title: "Advanced" negative-offset pagination always 500s: Django rejects negative slices
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and the client supplies a cursor with a negative offset (Cursor.from_string accepts e.g. "0:-5:0"), the code evaluates queryset[cursor.offset : cursor.offset + limit + extra]. Django's QuerySet raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported") for negative slice bounds, so the request errors with a 500. The comments above the branch are false: Django does not "properly handle negative slicing automatically", and the statement "This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level" is meaningless. This advertised feature cannot work as written and is reachable via a crafted cursor query parameter on the audit log endpoint.

findings.title: SET to ZSET type change on existing span-buf:s:* keys will cause WRONGTYPE errors during rolling deploys
findings.body: The PR changes the Redis type of the existing span-buf:s:{project_id:trace_id}:span_id keys from SET (sadd/sscan/sunionstore/scard) to ZSET (zadd/zscan/zunionstore/zcard/zpopmin) while keeping the exact same key names. Segment keys live up to redis_ttl (3600s) and consumers are upgraded in a rolling fashion, so old and new code will operate on the same keys concurrently: old consumers' SADD/SSCAN against newly created ZSET keys, and new consumers' ZADD/ZCARD/ZPOPMIN/ZSCAN against SET keys created minutes earlier, both raise redis WRONGTYPE errors. That crashes span processing and flushing and drops spans. The migration needs a new key prefix or an explicit transition plan rather than reusing the live keyspace.

findings.title: Spans evicted by ZPOPMIN are dropped silently with no metric or log
findings.body: When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, the script now evicts the excess with ZPOPMIN, permanently discarding span payloads from the segment. The previous behavior (skip oversized segments at flush time) emitted the metric spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded and an error log; that check is removed from _load_segment_data in this PR, and the new eviction emits nothing: the script doesn't return the evicted count and process_spans records no metric. Operators lose all visibility into truncated segments and the associated data loss. Return the evicted count from the script and emit a metric/log from Python.

findings.title: max_segment_spans option is now dead; the cap is hardcoded to 1000 in Lua
findings.body: SpansBuffer.__init__ still accepts and stores max_segment_spans (default 1001), but the only remaining enforcement is a hardcoded `if span_count > 1000` in add-buffer.lua. The flush-time check that used self.max_segment_spans was removed from _load_segment_data, so configuring this option now silently does nothing (and the default 1001 doesn't even match the Lua 1000). Either pass the limit into the script as an ARGV or delete the parameter.

findings.title: Redirect resolution limit lowered 10000 to 1000; deep traces will silently split into multiple segments
findings.body: The redirect-following loop limit was reduced from 10000 to 1000 and the comment documenting the consequence ("segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly") was deleted. For trace trees deeper than 1000 redirects, the loop now stops early and the span is written to whatever set the partial resolution landed on, splitting one logical segment into multiple flushed segments (partial/duplicated output downstream). This tradeoff is 10x more reachable than before; if intentional for script latency, the consequence should stay documented and a metric should be emitted when the limit is actually hit.

findings.title: No test coverage for the eviction feature or the new paginator
findings.body: The headline behavior of this PR — capping segments at 1000 spans via ZPOPMIN during insert — has no test: the buffer tests were only updated to add the newly required end_timestamp_precise field. A test inserting more than 1000 spans into one segment should assert which spans survive (lowest end_timestamp_precise evicted), that the segment still flushes, and that TTLs are intact. Likewise, the new OptimizedCursorPaginator / audit-log optimized_pagination path has no tests at all; even a trivial smoke test would have caught that it 500s on the first page due to the datetime TypeError.

findings.title: Added comment falsely claims negative cursor offsets are supported
findings.body: The new comment in Cursor.__init__ says "Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios", but no code was changed and negative offsets are not actually usable: Django querysets raise ValueError on negative slices, and BasePaginator.get_result clamps negative next-cursor offsets to 0. This misdocuments the Cursor contract for anyone building on it and should be removed or corrected.
